fixes.explanation: Priests are a fair guess, friend. But the verse says the beloved of His soul is given into the hands of her enemies. (Jeremiah 12:7) That word enemies is the one to hold onto. It sounds heavy because it is.
Kings sound official, I'll give you that. But the LORD says He has given the beloved of His soul "…into the hands of her enemies." (Jeremiah 12:7) The verse says enemies, plain and simple.
Running away is what I'd do around a real lion, baker. But the verse gives a different action: "She has roared against Me…" (Jeremiah 12:8) Roaring is what this lion does, and it's aimed at Him.

Hiding is a quiet move, friend, and a roar is not. The LORD says His inheritance is like a lion in the forest, and "She has roared against Me…" (Jeremiah 12:8) That roar is what the verse gives us, so keep that sound in your head.

Kings are a fair guess, friend. But in this verse the command is, "Go, gather all the beasts of the field; bring them to devour her." (Jeremiah 12:9) The word is beasts, not kings. Hold onto the field and the beasts.

North is a fair guess, baker. But in this verse it's "…the sword of the LORD…" that devours "…from one end of the earth to the other." (Jeremiah 12:12) That covers a whole lot more than one direction.

Fasting is a fair guess, friend, but it isn't the word in this verse. The LORD says, "But if they will not obey, then I will uproot that nation; I will uproot it and destroy it, declares the LORD." (Jeremiah 12:17) The word we want is obey.
